x: Honeybees live together in a hive. A hive can have thousands of bees. The worker bees fly from flower to flower. They drink a sweet juice called nectar. Then they carry it back to the hive and turn it into honey. Bees also help flowers make seeds. When they visit a flower, they carry yellow dust called pollen to the next one. Without bees, we would have fewer apples, berries, and pumpkins.

Dear Grandpa,

Today our class learned about owls. Owls hunt at night, and they sleep in the day. They have big eyes, so they can see in the dark. An owl can turn its head very far to look behind it. Its feathers are soft, so it flies without making a sound. I drew a picture of a barn owl for you. I will bring it when we visit you in June.

Love, Nora

Elephants are the biggest animals that live on land. They use their long trunks in many ways. An elephant can pick up food, drink water, and spray dust on its back with its trunk. Elephants eat grass, leaves, fruit, and bark. They eat for many hours each day. Baby elephants stay close to their mothers. The whole family helps take care of them, so the babies are safe.

Our class has a hamster named Peanut. He is brown and white, and he has tiny pink feet. Every week, a different student takes care of him. Last week, it was my turn. I gave Peanut fresh water and food, and I cleaned his cage. At night, Peanut likes to run on his wheel. He stuffs seeds in his cheeks to save them for later. I was sad when my week ended, but I will get another turn soon.

Some things float in water, and some things sink. Our class did a test with a tub of water. We dropped in a cork, a coin, a leaf, and a rock. The cork and the leaf floated on top. The coin and the rock sank to the bottom. Big ships are very heavy, but they float because of their shape. Next week, we will make little boats out of foil and see which one holds the most pennies.

A shadow forms when something blocks light. In the morning, my shadow on the playground was very long. At lunch, the sun was high in the sky, and my shadow was short. After school, it was long again. My friend Jada and I made shadow shapes with our hands. She made a bird, and I made a dog. When a cloud covered the sun, our shadows went away.

Water can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas. Ice is solid water. It is hard, and it keeps its shape. The water in your cup is a liquid, so it takes the shape of the cup. When water boils, it turns into a gas called water vapor. You cannot see it, but it goes up into the air. Water changes from one form to another when it gets hotter or colder.

Your body has more than 200 bones. Bones hold you up and give your body its shape. Muscles are attached to bones, and they pull on them to make you move. When you run, jump, or wave, your muscles are working. Your heart is a muscle too. It pumps blood all day and all night. To keep your bones and muscles strong, eat healthy food, drink water, and play outside.

Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. People call it the Red Planet, because its dust and rocks are reddish. Mars is smaller than Earth, and it is much colder. It has the biggest volcano we know of in our solar system. Its name is Olympus Mons. Scientists have sent rovers to Mars. A rover is a robot car that drives around and takes pictures. Someday, people might visit Mars too.

The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it. As the Moon goes around Earth, we see different parts of its bright side. Sometimes we see a whole circle, and that is a full moon. Sometimes we see only a thin curve, and that is a crescent. It takes about a month for the Moon to go through all its shapes. I drew the Moon every night for two weeks, and I saw it change.

Dear Diary,

Today my family went to the planetarium. We sat in soft seats and looked up at a big round ceiling. The lights went off, and stars filled the dome. A guide showed us Saturn and its rings. She said Jupiter is the biggest planet, and it has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot. My brother liked the comets best, but I liked the part about the Sun. I want to go back next year.

The International Space Station flies high above Earth. Astronauts live and work there for months at a time. Inside, everything floats, so they strap themselves into sleeping bags at night. They drink from pouches, because water would float away from a cup. The station goes around Earth about 16 times every day. That means the astronauts can see many sunrises and sunsets.

A volcano is an opening in the ground. Deep under Earth's surface, it is so hot that rock melts. This melted rock is called magma. When a volcano erupts, the magma comes out, and then it is called lava. Lava is very hot, and it glows orange and red. When it cools, it turns into hard rock. Some islands, like the islands of Hawaii, were made by volcanoes over a very long time.

The sun warms the water in lakes, rivers, and oceans. Some of the water turns into a gas and rises into the sky. High up, the air is cool, so the gas turns back into tiny drops. The drops come together and make clouds. When the drops get big and heavy, they fall as rain or snow. Then the water flows back to the lakes and oceans. This is called the water cycle, and it happens again and again.

Many trees change with the seasons. In spring, small buds open into green leaves. In summer, the leaves are big, and the tree makes lots of shade. In fall, the leaves on some trees turn yellow, orange, and red. Then they drop to the ground. In winter, those trees have bare branches. Pine trees are different, because they keep their needles all year. That is why people call them evergreens.

On Saturday, the wind was very strong. It blew the leaves across our yard, and it made the trees bend. My brother and I took our kite to the hill. The wind lifted it high into the air. It flew higher than the tallest tree. Then a big gust pulled the string out of my hand. We chased the kite down the hill. Luckily, it landed in a bush, and we got it back.

Martin Luther King Jr. was a leader who worked to make laws fair for all people. He gave many speeches. In his most famous speech, he talked about his dream that all people would be treated the same. He believed in peaceful ways to make changes, and many people marched with him. Today, we remember him on a holiday in January. Our class read a book about his life, and then we wrote about our own dreams.

Sacagawea was a Shoshone woman who helped explorers long ago. In 1804, Meriwether Lewis and William Clark set out to explore the land in the West. In 1805, Sacagawea joined their trip with her baby son. She knew some of the land, and she spoke the Shoshone language. That helped the explorers talk to the people they met. Today, her picture is on a gold dollar coin.

The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor. It was a gift from the people of France to the United States. It was finished in 1886. The statue is a woman holding a torch high in her right hand. In her left hand, she holds a tablet. The statue is made of copper. It used to be shiny and brown, but now it is green. Visitors can climb the steps inside it all the way up to the crown.

Long ago, many children went to school in a one-room schoolhouse. Kids of all ages sat in the same room with one teacher. They did not have paper notebooks, so they wrote on small slates with chalk. In winter, a big stove kept the room warm. Some children walked a long way to get there. My class visited an old schoolhouse, and I got to ring the bell.

Japan is a country in Asia. It is made of many islands. Its biggest city is Tokyo, and it has very busy streets. Many people in Japan eat rice, fish, and noodles. They often eat with chopsticks. Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan, and it has snow on top for much of the year. In spring, people go to parks to see the pink cherry blossoms.

Most maps have a compass rose. It shows which way is north, south, east, and west. North is usually at the top of the map. On a map of the United States, Canada is to the north, and Mexico is to the south. The Atlantic Ocean is to the east, and the Pacific Ocean is to the west. I used a compass rose to find my way on a map of the zoo. The lions were east of the gate.

Dear Amara,

Thank you for your letter! I liked learning about Kenya. You said that you can see giraffes and zebras near your town. That is so cool. Here in Ohio, we see deer, squirrels, and lots of birds. It snowed last week, and I built a fort. Do you ever get snow? Please tell me about your school and your favorite food.

Your friend, Leo

The Great Wall of China is very long. It winds over mountains, hills, and deserts. People built it a long time ago to protect their land. Many workers added to it over hundreds of years. Some parts are made of stone and brick. Others are made of dirt that was pressed down hard. Today, lots of visitors come from around the world to walk on the wall.

This spring, my family started a garden in our backyard. First, we pulled out the weeds. Then we dug holes and planted tomatoes, carrots, and beans. My job is to water the plants after school. Last week, I saw the first red tomato. My mom picked it, and we cut it into slices. It tasted better than the tomatoes from the store. I can't wait to pick the carrots.

Here is how to make lemonade with a grown-up. First, cut four lemons in half. Then squeeze the juice into a big pitcher. Next, add half a cup of sugar and four cups of cold water. Stir it with a long spoon until the sugar is gone. Taste it to see if you need more sugar. Last, add some ice. Pour a glass for yourself and your friends, and enjoy it on a hot day.

On Tuesday, I could not find my lunchbox. I looked in my backpack, under my desk, and in the coat room. It was not there. My stomach started to growl. Then my friend Sofia asked if I had checked the bus. I ran to the office, and the bus driver had left it there for me. I was so happy. I said thank you, and then I ate my lunch with Sofia.

Every year, we go to my grandma's house for Thanksgiving. My aunts, uncles, and cousins come too. The house smells like turkey, bread, and pie. Before we eat, everyone says one thing they are thankful for. I said I was thankful for my cousins. After dinner, we played board games, and Grandpa told funny stories. It was late when we drove home, so I fell asleep in the car.

Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith. The first hoops were peach baskets! Today, two teams play on a court. Players bounce the ball, and that is called dribbling. They pass it to their teammates and try to shoot it through the hoop. A basket usually counts for two points. A shot from far away counts for three. My team practices on Tuesdays, and I am getting better at free throws.

Field Day was the best day of the year. Our whole school went outside to play games. First, we ran a sack race. I fell down once, but I got up and finished. Next, we had a relay race, and my team came in second. Then we played tug of war against the other second grade class. We pulled as hard as we could, and we won! After that, we ate frozen treats in the shade.

Chess is a game for two players. Each player has 16 pieces. There are pawns, rooks, knights, bishops, a queen, and a king. Each piece moves in its own way. The knight is the only piece that can jump over others. The goal is to trap the other player's king. My grandpa taught me how to play. At first, he won every game, but last night I beat him for the first time.

In winter, our town turns the park into an ice rink. Last Sunday, I went skating with my dad. My skates were tight, and my ankles felt wobbly. I held on to the wall and took small steps. Dad showed me how to glide on one foot and then the other. Soon I could skate without holding on. I fell two times, but I laughed and got back up. Then we drank hot cocoa to warm up.

In art class, we made pots out of clay. First, I rolled the clay into a ball. Then I pushed my thumbs into the middle to make a hole. I pinched the sides to make them thin and even. My teacher put our pots in a hot oven called a kiln. The heat made the clay hard. The next week, I painted my pot blue and green. Now it sits on our kitchen table, and Mom keeps her keys in it.

An orchestra is a big group of musicians who play together. The instruments are put into families. Violins and cellos are in the string family. Flutes and clarinets are in the woodwind family. Trumpets and tubas are brass, and drums are percussion. The leader is called the conductor. She stands in front and waves a thin stick called a baton. It helps everyone keep the same beat.

Our class wrote and made our own books. First, we thought of an idea for a story. My story was about a turtle who wanted to fly. Then I wrote the words on each page. Next, I drew pictures to go with them. I made the cover out of thick paper and used a stapler to hold it together. When we were done, we shared our books with the first graders. They laughed at my turtle.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was a famous composer. A composer is a person who writes music. Mozart was born in Austria in 1756. He started playing music when he was very young. By the time he was five, he was writing his own songs. When he grew up, he wrote more than 600 pieces of music. People around the world still play his music today.

Orville and Wilbur Wright were brothers who loved to build things. They had a shop where they fixed bikes. They also wanted to make a machine that could fly. They tested gliders for years. On December 17, 1903, they flew the first airplane with an engine at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. The first flight lasted only 12 seconds, but it changed the world. Today, planes carry people all over the globe.

Long ago, books were copied by hand. It took a very long time to make just one. Then, around 1440, a man named Johannes Gutenberg made a printing press in Germany. It used little metal letters that could be moved around to make words. Workers put ink on the letters and pressed paper on top. Now many copies of a page could be made fast. Soon books were cheaper, and more people learned to read.

A robot is a machine that can do jobs. A person writes instructions, called code, to tell the robot what to do. Some robots work in factories, and they put cars together. Some robots vacuum the floor. Others explore places that are hard for people to reach, like the bottom of the ocean or the surface of Mars. In our class, we built a small robot. We told it to move forward, turn left, and stop.

Pencils are simple tools, but they are very useful. The inside of a pencil is called the lead, but it is not really lead. It is made of graphite mixed with clay. When you press it on paper, tiny bits of graphite rub off and leave a mark. The outside is made of wood. Many pencils have an eraser on the end, so you can fix your mistakes. I use about three pencils every month at school.
